target_customer: Online shoppers wanting one feed of items from their favorite brands in their size and price range
problem: Shoppers browse many brand sites to find clothes that fit their size and budget; PerShop aimed to be one personal store.
business_model: Consumer app, planned targeted e-commerce advertising (per Crunchbase description)

founders.name: Amol Jain
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as co-founder of WorkWhile, a later company.

founders.name: Tony Dong
founders.background_notes: No bio on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A recommendation and catalog aggregation app; the hard part was getting brand product feeds, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: No data or network moat; retailers and marketplaces could build the same feed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes incumbent reaction; the YC page marks the company Inactive.

market_need_then: Online apparel was large and fragmented, but no source found documents demand for this specific product.

brand_strength.rationale: Only a trend blog and database listings mention the brand; no press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: PerShop was a two person Winter 2019 team building a personalized clothing shopping app. The YC directory lists it as Inactive, but no post-mortem, shutdown notice, or funding news was found, so the cause is not public. One founder later co-founded WorkWhile, which suggests the team moved on.
notes: The company website pershop.app did not resolve from this environment, so it is treated as unreachable, not confirmed dead. Dealroom lists an enterprise value of 2M but no rounds, so no round recorded. Searches for competitors returned only current B2B personalization vendors, so the list is empty. Founder roles other than names are not sourced.
